PullRequest.Title: Add Visual Studio-style column selection paste
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #5940 

## Summary

Implement Visual Studio-style block pasting for copied column selections, addressing the rectangular-paste behavior discussed in #5940. This intentionally does not implement virtual space. This PR adds a setting `editor.columnSelectionPaste` with values `block` (spread behavior) and `text` (default, existing paste behavior).

## Paste behavior in Visual Studio

| Destination Type | Block paste behavior |
| --- | --- |
| One empty selection | Insert successive copied rows on successive destination lines at the cursor's visible column. |
| One non-empty single-line selection | Replace the selection with the first row, then insert remaining rows on successive lines. |
| One continuous multi-line selection with a different row count | Replace the selection with the first row, then insert remaining rows on successive lines |
| One continuous multi-line selection with a matching selected-row count | Replace the selection with the first row, then insert remaining rows on successive lines |
| Multiple selections with a different count | Paste the full text into each destination, matching the proposal's Visual Studio comparison.  Replace each (if non-empty) selection by the first row of the copied text|
| Multiple selections matching the copied row count | Distribute one copied row per destination in document order. Replace each (if non empty) selection by the corresponding copied row |

## Current behavior in VS Code

The multi-cursor case is already covered in VS Code. When there are the same number of destination cursors as the number of copied rows and the setting `editor.multiCursorPaste` is `spread`, then the copied rows are spread on the destination rows. Otherwise if the count differs then the text is pasted at each cursor.

This PR covers the case when there is only one destination selection which VS Code currently does not cover.

## Manual verification checklist

Text to column copy

```
    "AA",
    "BB",
    "CC",
```

Text into which to paste

```
    "left--right",
    "left--right",
    "left--right",
```

- [x] With `editor.columnSelectionPaste` unset, confirm the default is `text` and copying a column selection then pasting at one cursor performs ordinary multiline insertion.
- [x] Set `editor.columnSelectionPaste` to `block`. Create a real column selection over `AA`, `BB`, and `CC` on three source lines (not three independently added cursors), and copy it. Paste at column 5 of three `left--right` lines. Expect `leftAA--right`, `leftBB--right`, and `leftCC--right`.
- [x] Switch from `block` to `text` and back without reloading. Confirm each paste immediately follows the selected mode.
- [x] Paste onto a non-empty single-line selection. Confirm the first copied row replaces the entire selection and remaining rows are inserted on successive lines at the selection start column.
- [x] Repeat with forward and reversed multiline selections shorter than, equal to, and taller than the copied block. Confirm the first row replaces the entire selection regardless of height; remaining rows go below the replacement, aligned to its starting column, and unselected prefix/suffix text survives.
- [x] Paste over short and empty destination lines, and near EOF. Confirm short lines receive alignment spaces and missing destination lines are appended without moving the first line’s suffix onto a later row.
- [x] Repeat with tabs, different tab sizes, combining characters, wide characters, and emoji before the insertion point. Confirm rows align by visible column.
- [x] Paste at multiple cursors/selections, with a matching copied-row count. Confirm existing multi-cursor distribution is retained rather than repeating a rectangular block at every cursor when `editor.multiCursorPaste` is `spread`. When it is `text` confirm the existing full text behavior. Each selection is replaced by the corresponding row.
- [x] Paste at multiple cursors/selections, with a non-matching copied-row count. Confirm the full text is pasted at every cursor. Each selection is replaced by the first row of the copied text.
- [x] Check insert and overtype modes with `editor.overtypeOnPaste` enabled/disabled. Confirm the existing overwrite rules apply and read-only editors remain unchanged.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-row cardinality and exact flag chain that disables the repository's OOM guard are directly traced. Runtime duration depends on document/decorations, but the allocation and coalescing regression is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-row edit, inverse-edit, undo, piece-tree, decoration-update, and content-change objects plus synchronous CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With R copied rows and enough existing destination lines, this loop creates R tracked edit operations; notebook mirroring can repeat that cost per one-selection tracked cell. Rows after EOF are coalesced, so the effective count is the copied rows that land on existing lines plus one append operation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Large temporary memory/GC pressure, blocked paste latency, and possible out-of-memory failure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A single-cursor multiline paste used one ReplaceCommand and therefore one tracked edit operation regardless of pasted row count.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Block mode invokes ReplaceCommand/ReplaceOvertypeCommand once per destination row, and both add a tracked edit. CommandExecutor marks the first operation _isTracked; PieceTreeTextBuffer then sets canReduceOperations=false, bypassing its >=1000-operation reduction that is explicitly documented as preventing OOM crashes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 48 newly adds one tracked model edit per block row; before this feature the single-selection paste path submitted one replacement for the entire text.
Findings.Title: Let large block pastes use the model's edit coalescing safeguard
Findings.Impact: Pasting a realistic 1,000-10,000-row column block into a large file keeps thousands of edits separate on the UI thread instead of collapsing them, producing a long freeze and potentially exhausting memory. The editor's default multiCursorLimit permits 10,000 source rows.
Findings.Evidence: The new loop calls ChosenReplaceCommand.getEditOperations at line 48 for every copied row that maps to an existing destination line. replaceCommand.ts uses builder.addTrackedEditOperation. CommandExecutor propagates hadTrackedEditOperation to filteredOperations[0]._isTracked. PieceTreeTextBuffer.applyEdits disables canReduceOperations on that flag; its _reduceOperations threshold is 1000 and its comment states that collapsing is required to avoid OOM from temporary allocations. The same buffer path also creates inverse operations, content changes, and per-change decoration updates.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not mark every row operation tracked. Use ordinary edit operations and compute the final cursor from a tracked selection or from the coalesced inverse range, or proactively collapse large block pastes into one equivalent contiguous edit while preserving undo and final-cursor semantics.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path, ordinary-selection fallback, and linear grapheme scans are explicit in the repository. Only prevalence of extremely long lines affects magnitude, not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread CPU spent slicing line prefixes and iterating grapheme boundaries
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For an ordinary selection, the added lookup scans both the selection-start and cursor-position prefixes, so cost grows with their column offsets even when only a few selected characters are copied.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Copy/cut latency and editor input jank on very long lines
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary copy/cut proceeded directly to getPlainTextToCopy, whose getValueInRange work was proportional to the selected range; it did not calculate visual columns.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every copy/cut now calls getCursorColumnSelectData().isReal. When the selection is not an active column selection, that getter constructs fallback data by calling visibleColumnFromColumn for both endpoints; each call substrings the prefix and walks it with GraphemeIterator.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 48 newly executes viewModel.getCursorColumnSelectData().isReal before getPlainTextToCopy for all copies, including non-column selections.
Findings.Title: Avoid computing visual columns for every ordinary copy
Findings.Impact: Copying a small token near the end of a multi-megabyte generated/minified line now synchronously scans that long prefix twice before clipboard data can be produced, visibly delaying Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X.
Findings.Evidence: The added line invokes CursorsController.getCursorColumnSelectData on every generateDataToCopy call. Ordinary setStates clears _columnSelectData, so the getter's fallback path runs; cursor.ts:285-296 calls cursorConfig.visibleColumnFromColumn twice. CursorColumns.visibleColumnFromColumn creates a prefix substring and iterates every grapheme. createClipboardCopyEvent calls generateDataToCopy synchronously from the DOM clipboard event, while getPlainTextToCopy reads only the selected model ranges.
Findings.Recommendation: Expose/read a cheap column-selection identity flag (for example an accessor that tests whether real column-select data exists) and only compute fallback visual coordinates for callers that actually need them.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copy or cut an ordinary non-column selection in the code editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The DOM copy/cut handler synchronously generates editor clipboard data before it can populate DataTransfer and return. The newly added block-state lookup is on this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize clipboard metadata and selected text into the DOM DataTransfer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per copy/cut event; metadata adds one boolean field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same clipboard serialization occurred, but generateDataToCopy did not query column-select data or scan cursor-line prefixes first.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the clipboard event returns; the existing serialization is unchanged except for the negligible boolean. The newly reported prefix scans occur before it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selection and cursor column offsets on their view lines. For a tiny selection near the end of a long generated/minified line, the new work scales with the full prefixes rather than selected text length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous main-thread handler; the two fallback visible-column scans run serially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or memoized visible-column index is used. Active real column-selection data is stored, but ordinary selection changes clear it and force the fallback calculations on each copy/cut.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ordinary selection state clears _columnSelectData, the fallback performs two linear grapheme scans, and the added line invokes it synchronously for every copy/cut.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long single lines are workload-dependent, but generated bundles, minified assets, and large JSON lines are realistic; exact delay varies with prefix size and grapheme composition.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable latency regression: the diff adds work proportional to unrelated line prefixes on every ordinary copy/cut.

Scenarios.Scenario: Paste a copied column selection as a block into one cursor in a normal editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Paste handling synchronously splits clipboard text, computes target columns, constructs edits, applies them to the piece tree, updates decorations, emits content changes, and computes the cursor before the editor responds.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective row count is copied rows that map to existing destination lines, plus at most one coalesced append edit after EOF. Source column selections can reach the default 10,000-cursor limit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous command on the main thread. Row scans and model edits are serial; there is no limiter or deferred chunking.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is relevant. Destination line contents and visual columns are read once per affected existing row; clipboard text is split once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: each row calls a tracked ReplaceCommand, CommandExecutor marks the operation set tracked, and PieceTreeTextBuffer consequently bypasses its >=1000 edit coalescing path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact freeze duration depends on row widths, decorations, listeners, and machine memory. The model's explicit 1,000-edit OOM safeguard establishes that keeping thousands of these edits separate is unsafe regardless of exact timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable memory and latency regression: the new block path defeats an existing OOM-prevention mechanism for realistic large blocks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Paste while notebook multi-cursor editing mirrors operations across cells
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The anchor editor handles its paste, then NotebookMultiCursorController iterates tracked cells synchronously and invokes each cell controller. Cells with exactly one destination selection and block mode execute the new row-wise block command; cells with multiple selections retain existing distributed/full paste behavior.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tracked-cell count multiplied by copied block rows for cells with one selection; effective per-cell edit cardinality is bounded by existing destination rows before the append coalescing branch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Strictly serial trackedCells.forEach; no shared limiter, queue, or yielding. This is existing fan-out, but propagating isBlock newly selects the heavier row-wise command in eligible mirrored cells.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No paste-result caching or cross-cell coalescing. Each cell has its own model and independently recomputes visual columns and edits.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call-path propagation and serial fan-out; moderate for how often many tracked cells each have exactly one selection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Notebook sessions often have multiple selections within a cell, which bypass block distribution, so prevalence of the multiplicative case is uncertain. The synchronous per-cell call path is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: The notebook change amplifies the reported large-block mechanism but does not warrant a separate finding because it is the same core tracked-edit issue and requires the narrower one-selection-per-cell state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary text-mode paste and platform/web clipboard paste routing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing platform paste trigger or web clipboardService.readText must complete before text reaches Handler.Paste. With no block metadata or the default columnSelectionPaste='text', the existing simple/distributed paste path remains on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Trigger platform paste or read text from the system clipboard
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trigger/read per paste invocation; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single clipboard trigger/read occurred; the payload omitted isBlock.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing clipboard operation must complete before the web fallback can paste. The new boolean metadata handling occurs afterward and adds no boundary call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse vscode-editor-data JSON metadata from DataTransfer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per browser paste event; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same JSON object was parsed without an isBlock field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous metadata parsing already occurred before dispatch. Reading the added boolean does not materially change serialization cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Clipboard byte length and destination cursor count, unchanged after metadata parsing; one additional boolean is propagated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing platform trigger/read is awaited once; editor edit application remains synchronous. The diff adds no parallel requests or retries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: In-memory clipboard metadata is a single-entry exact-text cache. The diff adds isBlock to that existing entry without changing keying, lifetime, hit/miss behavior, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from payload routing and the default option value.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the diff: the added payload field is constant-size, and default text mode does not enter the new row-wise command.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance regression in ordinary paste routing or clipboard boundaries; their cardinality and scheduling are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 20 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted two findings: synchronous full-prefix grapheme scans newly added to every ordinary copy/cut, and per-row tracked block-paste edits that disable the text buffer's explicit large-edit OOM coalescing safeguard. Clipboard IPC/serialization is unchanged; notebook propagation only multiplies the second mechanism in eligible mirrored cells.
